title: Evaluation and injective-cocycle normalization of supported Hom
statement:
Fix $A=A_{E,n}$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Work either on the small etale site or on the small pro-etale site, using small representatives in the coefficient universe, ordinary $A_X$-module sheaves, and constant coefficient modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P=i_*A_Z$, with underived direct image and the actual constant restriction $\rho:A_X\to P$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Define $S(M)=\Gamma_Z(X,M)=\ker(M(X)\to M(U))$, as in [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Regard its values and all Hom groups below as abelian groups. These module-sheaf categories have enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives].

For every module sheaf $M$, evaluation defines an additive natural isomorphism
$$\theta_M:\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}S(M),\qquad \theta_M(f)=(f\circ\rho)_X(1).$$
Under $\operatorname{Hom}(A_X,M)\cong M(X)$ and the open adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A_U,M)\cong M(U)$ for extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], precomposition by the open counit is exactly restriction $M(X)\to M(U)$. In particular the displayed $\theta$ is the isomorphism of this actual kernel, with no choice of an automorphism of $S$.

Use cochain complexes, the bounded-below derived category and integer shifts [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], with $P$ in degree zero. The canonical etale supported-Hom identification induced by [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], and the canonical pro-etale identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom], have the following normalization. For every bounded-below $F$, every bounded-below degreewise injective resolution $e:F\to I$, every $a\in\mathbf Z$, and every supported cocycle $s\in S(I^a)$, let $f_s:P\to I^a$ be the unique map with $(f_s\rho)(1)=s$. Then
$$\chi_{i,F}^a([s])=(Qe)[a]^{-1}\circ Q(f_s):P[0]\longrightarrow QF[a],$$
where $[s]$ is transported from $H^a(S(I))$ through the canonical derived-unit and resolution comparisons to $H_Z^a(X,F)$, and $Q(f_s)$ is the localized complex map $P[0]\to QI[a]$. Equivalently $\chi$ is obtained by deriving $\theta^{-1}:S\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ and applying the roof-normalized RHom comparison [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof]. This normalization is natural in $F$ and independent of the chosen resolution and cocycle representative. On the etale site it agrees with the shifted restriction-cone identification of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. No quasi-compactness of $U$, constructibility, finite-Tor condition, or purity assumption is required.

source.place: Section 9, Example 9.5 and Ext proof of Theorem 9.4, pp. 66–67; module-valued, bounded-below and pro-etale normalization made explicit in original item steps 4 and 6.

proof.text: Use the small representatives stipulated in the statement. The category of ordinary $A_X$-module sheaves is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], applied to the constant ring sheaf on either small site. It therefore has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. All subsequent derivations take place in this module-sheaf category, with values in abelian groups; no assertion that forgetting the $A$-action preserves injectives is needed.

For any module sheaf $M$, define $e_X:\operatorname{Hom}(A_X,M)\to M(X)$ by $g\mapsto g_X(1)$. Its inverse sends $m$ to the morphism with component $A_X(V)\to M(V)$, $b\mapsto b\,m|_V$. Semilinearity of restriction makes these components commute with restriction. Conversely, $g_V(b)=b\,g_V(1)=b\,g_X(1)|_V$, so they are inverse additive maps, natural in $M$. This uses exactly the module-sheaf definition and the unit of the constant ring sheaf. The identical calculation over $U$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A_U,j^{-1}M)$ with $M(U)$.

source.place: Section 9, Example 9.5, p. 66, and the Ext proof of Theorem 9.4, p. 67; explicit module-valued normalization written by the agent

proof.text: Write $\epsilon:j_!A_U\to A_X$ for the open counit. The adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] apply respectively in the etale and pro-etale topology. The adjunct of $g\epsilon$ is $j^{-1}g:j^{-1}A_X=A_U\to j^{-1}M$: the counit is adjunct to the identity, and the adjunction bijection is natural in its target. Evaluation at $1$ sends this to $g_U(1)=g_X(1)|_U$. Thus precomposition by this actual counit, under the evaluations just constructed, is the actual restriction map, without a scalar or sign.

source.place: Section 9, Example 9.5, p. 66, and the Ext proof of Theorem 9.4, p. 67; explicit module-valued normalization written by the agent

proof.text: On the etale site apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $A_X$; its maps are the open counit $\epsilon$ and the closed unit $\rho$. The canonical constant-ring pullback identification of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1) gives $i^{-1}A_X=A_Z$ and identifies this unit with the stated constant restriction. On the pro-etale site [lem-pur-proetale-supported-constant-presentation] states directly that the same $\rho$ is a cokernel of $\epsilon$. For $s\in S(M)$, the preceding steps give a unique $g_s:A_X\to M$ with $g_s(1)=s$, and $g_s\epsilon=0$ because its adjunct evaluates to $s|_U=0$. The cokernel property gives a unique $f_s:P\to M$ with $f_s\rho=g_s$. Conversely $f\rho\epsilon=0$ implies $(f\rho)(1)|_U=0$. These constructions are inverse, proving $\theta$. Uniqueness of factorization proves additivity and naturality: $f_{s+t}=f_s+f_t$ and $f_{S(u)s}=u f_s$. Hence this is the specified kernel isomorphism, rather than an unspecified natural automorphism of $S$.

source.place: Section 9, Example 9.5, p. 66, and the Ext proof of Theorem 9.4, p. 67; explicit module-valued normalization written by the agent

proof.text: Put $v=\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ and $t=\theta^{-1}:S\to v$. Applied termwise, $t_I:S(I)\to v(I)$ is an isomorphism of cochain complexes: naturality of $t$ for $d_I^r$ says $t_{I^{r+1}}S(d_I^r)=v(d_I^r)t_{I^r}$. In particular a supported cocycle $s$ is sent to $f_s$, and $d_I^a f_s=0$. If $s$ changes by $S(d_I^{a-1})(b)$, then $f_s$ changes by $d_I^{a-1}f_b$, a coboundary in $v(I)$. These are equalities in the complexes themselves, with no comparison choice.

source.place: Section 9, Example 9.5, p. 66, and the Ext proof of Theorem 9.4, p. 67; explicit module-valued normalization written by the agent

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] for $S$ and $v$, writing their derived units as $\alpha_S$ and $\alpha_v$. Its universal property applied to $\alpha_v\circ Q(t)$ defines a unique $Rt:RS\to Rv$ satisfying $(Rt)_{QL}\alpha_{S,L}=\alpha_{v,L}Q(t_L)$. Doing the same with $t^{-1}$, uniqueness makes the two composites identities. Thus $Rt$ is a natural isomorphism. For a specified $e:F\to I$, put $c_{S,e}=(RS(Qe))^{-1}\alpha_{S,I}$ and $c_{v,e}=(Rv(Qe))^{-1}\alpha_{v,I}$. The units on $I$ are isomorphisms by clause (2) of that lemma, and naturality gives $(Rt)_{QF}c_{S,e}=c_{v,e}Q(t_I)$. This proves directly that deriving $t$ carries the class transported from $s$ to the class transported from $f_s$.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), and 070I (lemma-K-injective); explicit normalization written by the agent

proof.text: The given bounded-below degreewise injective $I$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Apply [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] in the abelian category of module sheaves, with $M=P$, $K=F$, $\varepsilon=e$, and integer $n=a$. It sends the class transported from $f_s$ by $c_{v,e}$ to $(Qe)[a]^{-1}\circ Q(f_s)$. The preceding step therefore gives the required formula for the composite $\chi^a_{i,F}=\psi^a_{QF}\circ H^a((Rt)_{QF})$. This realizes the supported-Hom isomorphism with exactly the evaluation normalization on the pro-etale site and the same construction on the etale site. The complex map corresponding to $f_s$ has its sole nonzero component in degree zero; the cochain convention $(I[a])^0=I^a$ introduces no sign into that component.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), and 070I (lemma-K-injective); explicit normalization written by the agent

proof.text: The map just defined is natural in $F$ because both $Rt$ and the isomorphisms $\psi^a$ of [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] are natural. Explicitly for $u:QF\to QG$, naturality gives $\chi^a_{i,G}H^a(RS(u))=u[a]\circ\chi^a_{i,F}$. It is defined on $H^a(RS(QF))$ without choosing $e$ or $s$. Since the roof calculation applies to every specified $e$, any two resolutions yield the same value after their canonical derived-unit comparisons. Step 5 shows directly that a coboundary change of $s$ does not change its transported class. This proves both independence assertions, including for negative $a$.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), and 070I (lemma-K-injective); explicit normalization written by the agent

proof.text: For the etale cone comparison set $E=I(X)$, $B=I(U)$ and $r:E\to B$ equal to restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact], $\epsilon:j_!A_U\to A_X$ is a monomorphism. For each injective $I^q$, its defining extension property [def-sp-injective-resolutions] makes $\operatorname{Hom}(A_X,I^q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A_U,I^q)$ surjective. Steps 2--4 identify this map with $r^q$, and its kernel with $S(I^q)=v(I^q)$. Moreover $j^{-1}I^q$ is injective: $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]; for a monomorphism $N\to N'$ on $U$, apply $j_!$, extend a map $j_!N\to I^q$ to $j_!N'$, then transpose by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. The exactness assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3) ensures $j^{-1}e$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently the bounded-below complexes $E$ and $B$ compute respectively $R\Gamma(X,F)$ and $R\Gamma(U,j^{-1}F)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. The comparison arrow $r$ is their actual derived restriction, since it is restriction in every degree.

source.place: Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); Modules on Sites Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); Derived Categories Tags 05TH and 05TI

proof.text: Now apply [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] to $r:E\to B$. Its specified comparison is $\kappa:S(I)\to\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$, $s\mapsto(0,s)$, and it is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the cone realization of $R\operatorname{Hom}(P,F)$ in [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] is, on this resolution, the map $v(I)\xrightarrow{\theta_I}S(I)\xrightarrow{\kappa}\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$. To see the normalization, realize the Hom triangle by the short exact sequence of complexes from Step 9. Its canonical map to the shifted cone is inclusion in the shifted source summand: in degree $q$ it sends $f:P\to I^q$ to $(0,(f\rho)(1))$. Steps 2--4 identify this with $\kappa\theta_I$. This computes the comparison itself, rather than inferring it merely from its composite to $E$. A supported cocycle is represented there by $(0,s)$; applying the inverse comparison and then the roof comparison gives $f_s$ and the roof of Step 7. The shifted cone differential is $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_By-r(x),d_Ex)$ as specified in the kernel-cone lemma, so $(0,s)$ has exactly the asserted sign. This identifies the etale restriction-cone normalization with the same $\chi$. Only the etale argument used that $\epsilon$ is monic; the pro-etale evaluation and roof arguments used just the cokernel presentation, which explicitly requires no quasi-compactness of $U$. No other finiteness or purity hypothesis has entered.
